name: Private 5G and industrial wireless
summary: Organizations operate dedicated wireless networks to connect machines, vehicles and workers with controlled coverage and service levels.
useCase: A port connects cranes and autonomous vehicles over a private mobile network with engineered coverage, identity and operational support.
whyNow: Private LTE/5G is becoming easier to buy, but deployment economics remain site-specific. GSA counted 2,031 customer organizations in 88 countries by Q2 2026. Its catalog spans LTE and 5G, pilots and commercial deployments, so it should not be treated as a census of live 5G-only factories. Recent customer additions slowed, making a selective growth story more credible than a universal replacement for Wi-Fi.

mainstream.scope: A routine connectivity option for large industrial campuses with coverage, mobility or reliability requirements that justify dedicated mobile infrastructure.
mainstream.rationale: A growing reference base supports mainstream procurement in ports, mines, utilities and complex factories. Growth is slower than early expectations, and supplier portfolios are changing. The window assumes lower integration costs and clear service-level advantages. Smaller sites may continue to prefer Wi-Fi or managed public networks.

direction: Growing, but customer additions have slowed

metric.name: Organizations in GSA’s private-mobile-network database
metric.scope: Reported private LTE/5G references, generally projects above €100,000; GSA coverage is incomplete and revised.
metric.growthLabel: Catalog expanded from 1,077 to 2,031 reported customers
metric.limitations: Customer references are not all live sites, unique networks, 5G-only deployments or the entire market. Dates differ within years, database discovery can revise past coverage and small projects are omitted. This series does not justify a precise market CAGR.
metric.futureNote: No consistent customer-reference forecast is used. The scenario assumes continued selective expansion rather than extrapolating the early catalog growth rate.

maturity.note: Analyst ordinal assessment, not an adoption percentage: 0 research, 1 proof of concept, 2 pilots, 3 commercial niche, 4 routine use in the stated market, 5 established/expanding. Future values are a scenario.

milestones.text: No comparable year-end measurement supplied; early private LTE should not be relabeled as 5G-only deployment.
GSA subsequently reported 1,077 customer organizations for the end of 2022.
The database reached 1,384 customer organizations at year end.
GSA reported 1,427 organizations at the end of Q1, not a full-year total.
No clean year-end value is inserted here because catalog revisions complicate the annual bridge.
GSA reached 2,031 organizations in Q2; Nokia agreed to sell Enterprise Campus Edge, with closing planned for H1 2027.

tailwinds: Industrial mobility and difficult radio environments reward engineered coverage.
Integrated edge compute can keep time-sensitive operational data close to equipment.
bottlenecks: Spectrum rules, radio planning, compatible devices and operational integration add cost.
Wi-Fi and public-network alternatives can provide sufficient performance more cheaply.
watchMetrics: New paying production sites and expansions, separated from pilots and catalog discoveries.
Total cost per connected asset, uptime, handover reliability and measured operational savings.
